concepts.title: Sources of Data: Primary and Secondary
concepts.definition: Data for geographic study come from primary sources collected in the field by the researcher through surveys, interviews and observation, and secondary sources already compiled by others such as the Census of India, National Sample Survey and government registers.
concepts.key_idea: Primary data fit the exact question asked but cost time; secondary data are cheap and comparable but may not match the study's needs.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy301.txt primary and secondary data sources and census-NSS references
question_patterns: distinguish primary and secondary sources of data
name the major secondary sources for Indian geography
what methods collect primary data in the field
why is the census a key secondary source
evaluate the reliability of secondary data
give examples of government registers as data sources

solution_steps.explain: field-collected data are primary; census and survey records are secondary
primary data cost effort but fit the purpose exactly
secondary series like census decades allow long-run comparison

concepts.title: Compilation and Tabulation of Data
concepts.definition: Compilation arranges collected figures into tables with title, columns of head notes, stub and caption, source note; data are first classified into categories and then entered systematically so that analysis becomes possible.
concepts.key_idea: The percentage share of any item in a table equals the part value times one hundred divided by the total value.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy301.txt compilation, tabulation parts and percentage calculation
question_patterns: list the parts of a statistical table
compute the percentage share of a table item
how is data classified before tabulation
what goes into the caption and stub of a table
why must a table carry a source note
differentiate qualitative and quantitative classification

solution_steps.explain: multiply the ratio by one hundred

concepts.title: Census and National Sample Survey as Sources
concepts.definition: The Census of India gives a complete decennial count of population, houses and economic activity, while the National Sample Survey Organisation collectives representative household data on consumption, employment and land holding through periodic rounds; both anchor secondary geographic analysis.
concepts.key_idea: Census gives completeness, NSS gives depth - together they cover most socio-economic questions a geographer asks.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy301.txt census rounds and National Sample Survey description
question_patterns: what does the Census of India record and how often
what does the National Sample Survey collect
compare complete enumeration with sample surveys
why are census decades useful for trend study
state limitations of census data for detailed analysis
which agency runs the National Sample Survey

solution_steps.explain: census enumerates all households; NSS samples representative ones
density and literacy come from census; consumption patterns from NSS rounds
ten-year census and survey rounds frame India's data timeline

concepts.title: Presentation Modes of Data
concepts.definition: Compiled data may be presented as tables, graphs, diagrams and maps; the choice depends on the nature of data and purpose - tables give exactness, graphs show trends, maps show spatial distribution.
concepts.key_idea: Choosing the right presentation mode turns numbers into arguments a reader can see.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy301.txt presentation of data modes discussion
question_patterns: list the modes of presenting data
when is a table preferable to a graph
why are maps chosen for spatial data
match data type with presentation mode
what makes a graph communicative
give an example of map presentation of census data

solution_steps.explain: tables, graphs, diagrams and maps are the presentation choices
trend questions need graphs, location questions need maps
the mode must serve the message, not decorate it

worked_examples.question_pattern: A district records 4,80,000 literates out of a population of 12,00,000. Compute the percentage share of literates.
Classify these into primary and secondary sources: field questionnaire, Census of India, village interview, NSS report.

solution_template.explain: field questionnaire and village interviews are collected by the researcher
Census and NSS reports are compiled by agencies
the first two fit the exact question, the second two give comparability

worked_examples.question_pattern: Choose a presentation mode for three data types: temperature trend, land-use shares, soil texture regions.

solution_template.explain: a line graph shows the temperature trend over years
a pie diagram displays land-use shares
a choropleth map shows soil texture regions
